Sam Chen: Pushed a proto for soft-eviction during batch admission to reduce KV OOMs. Canary results: OOMs down ~4x, but p99 token latency increased ~12%. attaching flame graphs and a quick diff. https://redwood-internal/ci/18425 :thinking:

Ria Patel: nice. what's the admission logic? hard-evict or gradual?

Sam Chen: soft-evict = mark low-reuse KV entries as "evict-candidate" and allow batches that exceed token budget by up to 6% while triggering background async evict. admission code here:
```python
def admit(batch):
    budget = estimate_kv_budget(batch)
    if current_kv + batch.kv_needed <= budget:
        return True
    if can_soft_evict(batch) and (batch.tokens <= budget*1.06):
        mark_candidates(batch)
        schedule_async_eviction()
        return True
    return False
```

Marco Diaz: interesting. we saw similar tail increase when matmul kernel update landed — memory fragmentation + async GC on device. did you correlate with kernel selection changes?

Sam Chen: good call — I repro'd on the canary that when "fast32_ker" was used for bigger batches kernel alloc pattern changed. flame graphs show spikes in cudaMalloc/free during batch assembly.

Anya Koval: maybe use a preflight estimator: run quick prefix scan for kv footprint and reject if estimated live_kv > threshold. avoids starting heavy kernels. also consider shedding tokens from low-priority requests.

Marco Diaz: +1 on token-shedding. We can drop speculative prefixes or reply faster with "partial" results. tradeoff is quality.

ci-bot: canary run 2026-06-14T08:12:07Z summary: OOMs 8->2, p50 latency -3%, p95 +4%, p99 +12%. tests: batch_admission_soft_eviction_A vs baseline. artifacts: ci://artifacts/18425/soft-evict

Ria Patel: what's the tunable? 6% soft-budget? what about candidate selection policy — LRU vs reuse-score?

Sam Chen: current proto uses reuse_score = kv.access_count / (now - kv.last_used) ; candidates chosen below threshold. trying LRU next.

Marco Diaz: propose combining soft-evict with kernel-aware admission: if kernel==fast32_ker and batch.tokens>128 then tighten soft budget to 2% (avoid fragmentation). also add a backoff counter per GPU to throttle admission when eviction backlog > X.

Anya Koval: add a tiny probe to run allocator_fragmentation_metric() before admitting large batches. if frag>0.25 then deny or force synchronous eviction.

Sam Chen: plan: roll soft-evict -> A/B split 10/90, compare p99, OOMs, and fragmentation metric. I'll open a follow-up run later today. @Marco Diaz @Anya Koval can you pair on the kernel-aware tweak?

Marco Diaz: I'll take the kernel gating.

Anya Koval: taking the probe + shed work. will post perf patch by EOD.

Sam Chen: thanks :rocket:
